additions.reason: Shame in Torah #28 is explicitly equated with idolatry using bechina language: 'בּוּשָׁה נִקְרֵאת עֲבוֹדַת אֶלִילִים' (line 6). The word 'נִקְרֵאת' (is called) is standard bechina language — shame IS idolatry. The source text further reinforces this: 'כִּי הַבּוּשָׁה וְהַחֵרוּף נַעֲשֶׂה מֵהַכְּפִירוֹת' (shame and disgrace come from heresy), identifying shame as the manifestation of heresy/idolatry. Shame (בושה) belongs in the evil Package 3 alongside כפירות and עבודה זרה as all three are aspects of the same sitra-achra reality: rejecting/mocking God-fearers.
additions.source_quote: וּבִשְׁבִיל זֶה בּוּשָׁה נִקְרָא עֲבוֹדַת אֶלִילִים, כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב (הושע ט): וַיִּנָּזְרוּ לַבֹּשֶׁת, כִּי הַבּוּשָׁה וְהַחֵרוּף נַעֲשֶׂה מֵהַכְּפִירוֹת

additions.reason: The lamb (כֶּבֶשׂ) of the daily tamid offering is explicitly identified in Torah #28 as a bechina: 'הַתָּמִיד כֶּבֶשׂ, כִּי מִמֶּנּוּ נִתְתַּקְּנוּ הָאַלְפִין, בִּבְחִינַת (ירמיה יא): וַאֲנִי כְּכֶבֶשׂ אַלּוּף' and 'זֶה בְּחִינַת כֶּבֶשׂ – שֶׁכָּבוּשׁ תַּחַת יַד רַבּוֹ וּמְשַׁמֵּשׁ אוֹתָם'. The lamb IS the one who is subdued under his master — it is equated (via בבחינת) with the tamid, the holy rectification. The כבש belongs in Package 1 (good) as it is another expression of the holy worm/faith/chesed cluster: the lamb = the one who is submissive and serves his teacher = the חסד/אמונה axis. Note: 'כבש' in this context plays on both 'lamb' and 'כבש = subdued', making it a bechina of humble service under a true sage.

additions.reason: The evil worm (תולע דקלפה) is the direct negative mirror of the holy worm (תולע דקדושה = Package 1). The source text states: 'וְיֵשׁ כְּנֶגְדּוֹ בַּקְּלִפָּה תּוֹלָע אֲשֶׁר מְכַלֶּה וְאוֹכֵל הַכֹּל' — there IS in the kelipah a worm that devours all. The post-text commentary (line 34) calls this 'תּוֹלָע דִּקְלִפָּה' as the explicit evil counterpart. This node is already in the dataset as node2_id in a Torah-28 eitza edge (id 1804: 'תולע [good] → מכניע תולע דקלפה'), but it is NOT in any bechina edge for Torah #28. It shares essential nature with עבודה זרה and כפירות: all three are aspects of the sitra achra's claim — the evil consuming/devouring force that the תולע דקדושה must subdue.

additions.reason: The harsh judgments of Leah (דינין קשים שבלאה) are the evil-side mirror of Package 2's holy Leah. Source text (line 33): 'כִּי הֵם יוֹנְקִים מֵהַדִּינִים הַקָּשִׁים שֶׁבְּלֵאָה, שֶׁמִּשָּׁם אֲחִיזַת הַקְּלִפּוֹת הַקָּשׁוֹת שֶׁהֵם בְּחִינַת עֲבוֹדָה זָרָה הַנַּ"ל'. The harsh judgments of Leah ARE (bechina language: 'שֶׁהֵם בְּחִינַת') the klipot/idolatry. While the source uses בחינת here in a slightly more complex sense (as the source of the klipot), the teaching makes clear that the harsh judgments of Leah are structurally equivalent to the evil domain. This is the evil aspect of Package 2's Leah: the same partzuf seen from its aspect of severe judgment rather than holy receptivity. Proposed as a separate negative addition to Package 2's conceptual domain, since Package 2 is the holy side of Leah. It could alternatively be assigned to Package 3 (evil domain), but its natural home is as the shadow-side of the Leah package.

analysis_notes.structural_note: Torah #28 is unusual in that its primary 8 bechina edges form 4 disconnected components. The teaching's deep structure requires the reader to recognize that CC-D (עולת תמיד / תולעת יעקב) is the ritual dimension of CC-A (אמונה / חסד / אברהם / תולע) — but this cross-component bechina connection is stated in the commentary text (lines 29-35), not in a formally encoded bechina edge. The merge of CC-D into CC-A is therefore text-justified but requires annotation.
analysis_notes.good_evil_mirror_structure: Torah #28 follows the standard mirror structure. Package 1 (אמונה/חסד/תולע — holy worm) mirrors the evil תולע דקלפה (Package 3 addition). Package 2 (לאה holy side) mirrors the דינין קשין של לאה (Package 2's own shadow, which feeds Package 3). Package 3 (כפירות/עבודה זרה) is the evil counterpart to Package 1's faith.
